html:
The Cry of Dolores was the call to revolt made by the priest Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla in the town of Dolores, central Mexico, early on 16 September 1810. It began the Mexican War of Independence.

Hidalgo, a creole parish priest, had joined a plot of creoles against Spanish rule. When it was discovered, he rang his church bell and called his parishioners to rise. Tens of thousands of Indigenous and mestizo peasants and miners joined him, marching under a banner of Our Lady of Guadalupe. They took Guanajuato, killing the Spaniards who had taken refuge in its granary.

The rebels came close to Mexico City but turned back. Hidalgo was captured in 1811 and shot. The struggle went on under José María Morelos and others, part of the independence wars, until Mexico became independent in 1821. Each 15 September the president repeats the cry from the National Palace.
